decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 1% to 1.25%. The vote was 9-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate despite hurricane-related disruptions.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Although the hurricanes caused a drop in payroll employment in September, the unemployment rate declined further.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising moderately so far this year.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Job gains have remained solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Gasoline prices rose in the aftermath of the hurricanes, boosting overall inflation in September; however, inflation for items other than food and energy remained soft.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, both inflation measures have declined this year and are running below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined this year and are running below 2 percent.”

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate despite hurricane-related disruptions.
The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.
On a 12-month basis, both inflation measures have declined this year and are running below 2 percent.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.77% APR costs about $53.21 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.37% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.88% would fall by about $1.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.3%, and employers added an average of 142k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (September 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.16%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.01% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 84%, cut 0%, hike 16%.

citations.detail: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.
